issues.description: TTSModelConfig.default_speaker for v3-beta is 'shubh' but documentation, PR description, and SarvamTTSSpeakerV3 enum order all declare 'aditya' as the default
issues.detail: The specification is contradicted by the implementation: the module docstring, class docstring, and PR text all say aditya is the v3-beta default; the dataclass sets 'shubh'. A reader cannot derive the postcondition (which speaker is selected when voice_id is None) from any single source. TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best; more likely a silent regression for any user relying on documented defaults.

issues.description: Pace validation silently clamps user input rather than refusing it, violating the precondition contract
issues.detail: InputParams declares pace ge=0.3, le=3.0 at the pydantic layer, then __init__ silently clamps to the model-specific subrange with only a warning. The precondition is therefore unstated: callers cannot tell whether out-of-range pace is rejected, clamped, or accepted. Either reject (raise ValueError, as done for unsupported model) or narrow the Field bounds. Do not do both half-heartedly. DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for a real specification.

issues.description: Equality comparison against pydantic defaults (params.pitch != 0.0) cannot distinguish 'user passed 0.0' from 'user passed nothing'
issues.detail: The warnings 'pitch parameter is ignored for {model}' fire only when the value differs from the hardcoded default, and never when a user explicitly passes the default value on v3. Conversely, a user who never touched pitch will never be warned, which is correct only by accident. The invariant 'warn iff user supplied an unsupported parameter' is not maintained. Use a sentinel or model_fields_set.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently substitutes v2 speakers for any unknown model, masking caller errors
issues.detail: The function accepts an unconstrained str and, on miss, returns v2 speakers with no diagnostic. This is a smuggled goto around the validation that __init__ performs: a caller using this helper to validate a speaker against a misspelled model receives a plausible but wrong list. Raise on unknown model, or return Optional[List[str]]. Do not invent a default.

issues.description: STT connect_kwargs drops input_audio_codec entirely; the previous behavior was to send it
issues.detail: The pre-PR connect payload included 'input_audio_codec': self._input_audio_codec. The refactored payload removes it without comment in the diff. If the underlying SDK derives codec from this field, this is a silent behavior change for all existing saarika:v2.5 and saaras:v2.5 deployments. State the precondition: is the codec now implicit, or was this an oversight? The diff offers no proof either way.

issues.description: Speaker name is never validated against the model's allowed speaker tuple
issues.detail: TTSModelConfig.speakers is computed and stored but never consulted in __init__. A user passing voice_id='anushka' with model='bulbul:v3-beta' is accepted, sent to the API, and fails at request time rather than construction time. The invariant 'voice_id in self._config.speakers' would catch this at the earliest possible moment. As written, the data is decorative.

review.summary: The refactor to dataclass-driven model configs is an improvement in form but the discipline is incomplete. Specifications are contradicted by data (v3-beta default speaker), preconditions are stated in two layers that disagree (pace bounds in pydantic vs. clamping in __init__), and warnings are gated on default-value comparison rather than on whether the user supplied the parameter — an invariant that holds only by coincidence. The STT side silently drops input_audio_codec from the connect payload with no justification in the diff; that is a behavior change presented as a refactor. REASONED in structure, UNREASONED in detail. Resolve the spec/code contradictions and decide whether out-of-range parameters are refused or clamped — pick one.
